package.name: airtable
package.packageFile:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/package.schema.json

# FULLY DECLARATIVE. Three nodes, one base URL, one token.
#
# This package forced TWO executor capabilities, both loops a manifest cannot write itself:
# `paginate` for reading past the first page, and `chunk` for writing a collection when the
# vendor caps a batch at ten. Every list-returning and collection-writing node after this
# one inherits both.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/airtable/`.

name: airtable
displayName: Airtable
description: Read, check and write Airtable records
version: 2.0.0
category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1775377626/gravity/icons/airtable.png

features:
  - Fetch records with filters, views and sorting, paginated
  - Check whether a value already exists
  - Insert and update records, batched and deduplicated

allowedHosts:
  - api.airtable.com

requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json]
  paginate: [cursor]
  chunk: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.3.0"

credentials.airtableCredential.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/credential.schema.json

name: airtableCredential
displayName: Airtable
description: Airtable Personal Access Token for reading and writing to Airtable bases
documentationUrl: https://airtable.com/create/tokens

properties:
  - name: personalAccessToken
    displayName: Personal Access Token
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Airtable Personal Access Token
    placeholder: pat

shared.rows.yaml:
# The row-splitting expressions, defined ONCE and $ref'd wherever they are needed.
#
# `AirtableInsert` needs "which rows are updates" and "which rows are creates" in three
# places each: the call's `when`, its `chunk.items`, and the skipped count in events. The
# sandbox has no assignment, so there is no way to bind an intermediate value inside an
# expression. A shared fragment is how one definition serves all three, and it is why these
# live here rather than being pasted six times.

# An Airtable record id is "rec" plus 14 characters. A row carrying one is an UPDATE.
isAirtableId: &isAirtableId >-
  return (config.records || []).filter(r =>
    typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec')

# Everything else is a CREATE. `id` is RESERVED by Airtable, so a row carrying its own
# non-Airtable `id` has it renamed to `apollo_id` rather than dropped: the retired code did
# this, and changing it would silently lose a column.
#
# Then anything the dedup field says is already in the table is removed. `calls.existing` is
# the paged read; when dedup is off that call is skipped and there is no key, so the filter
# passes everything through.
toCreate: &toCreate >-
  return (config.records || [])
    .filter(r => !(typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec'))
    .map(r => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(r).map(e => [e[0] === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : e[0], e[1]])))
    .filter(r => !String(config.dedupField || '').trim()
      || !((calls.existing || {}).items || [])
           .map(x => String(((x.fields || {})[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField]) ?? ''))
           .filter(Boolean)
           .includes(String(r[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField] ?? '')))

# Offered minus kept: how many the dedup field dropped.
skipped: &skipped >-
  return (config.records || [])
    .filter(r => !(typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec'))
    .length
  - (calls.creates ? calls.creates.sent : 0)

# The same set, as a boolean, for the call's `when`. Defined next to it so the two cannot
# drift: a `when` that disagreed with `items` would either skip a needed write or send an
# empty one.
toCreateAny: &toCreateAny >-
  return (config.records || [])
    .filter(r => !(typeof r.id === 'string' && r.id.length === 17 && r.id.slice(0, 3) === 'rec'))
    .filter(r => !String(config.dedupField || '').trim()
      || !((calls.existing || {}).items || [])
           .map(x => String(((x.fields || {})[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField]) ?? ''))
           .filter(Boolean)
           .includes(String(r[config.dedupField === 'id' ? 'apollo_id' : config.dedupField] ?? '')))
    .length > 0
shared.table.yaml:
# Everything the three nodes share: the auth, and the url for one table.
#
# The table part may be a NAME ("Companies") or an id ("tbl..."), so it is percent-encoded.
# The base id never needs encoding.

credential: &credential
  scheme: bearer
  token: "{{ credentials.airtableCredential.personalAccessToken }}"

url: &url >-
  return 'https://api.airtable.com/v0/' + config.baseId
    + '/' + encodeURIComponent(config.tableId)

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# A paginated call's reply is { items, pages, truncated }, so both rows read `items`.
#
# Dedup is expressed as "keep the first index for this value", because the sandbox has no
# assignment and therefore no seen-set. Same result, no mutation.

- emit: records
  from: response
  value: >-
    return response.items
      .map(r => Object.assign({ id: r.id }, r.fields || {}))
      .filter((r, i, all) => !config.dedupField
        || (String(r[config.dedupField] ?? '') !== ''
            && all.findIndex(x => String(x[config.dedupField] ?? '') === String(r[config.dedupField] ?? '')) === i))

- emit: totalCount
  from: response
  value: >-
    return response.items
      .map(r => Object.assign({ id: r.id }, r.fields || {}))
      .filter((r, i, all) => !config.dedupField
        || (String(r[config.dedupField] ?? '') !== ''
            && all.findIndex(x => String(x[config.dedupField] ?? '') === String(r[config.dedupField] ?? '')) === i))
      .length
files.api/run.yaml:
# One call in the manifest, as many requests as the table needs.
#
# Airtable returns up to 100 rows and an `offset` when there are more. `paginate` walks that
# until the offset is absent or maxRecords is reached, and hands back the accumulation.
#
# `fields[]` repeats for each name, which a query object cannot express as one key. It is
# built as a single pre-joined parameter instead, which the vendor accepts.

- name: page
  method: GET
  url: { $ref: table#url }
  credential: { $ref: table#credential }
  query:
    # Omitted when blank: the executor drops a key whose value resolved to nothing, and
    # Airtable rejects an empty formula rather than ignoring it.
    filterByFormula: "{{ config.filterFormula }}"
    view: "{{ config.view }}"
    # A page is never larger than the vendor's 100, nor than what is still wanted.
    pageSize: "return String(Math.min(config.maxRecords || 100, 100))"
    sort[0][field]: "{{ config.sortField }}"
    sort[0][direction]: "return config.sortField ? (config.sortDirection || 'asc') : ''"
    fields: >-
      return String(config.fields || '').split(',').map(f => f.trim()).filter(Boolean).join(',')
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
  paginate:
    strategy: cursor
    cursor: "return response.offset"
    into: offset
    items: "return response.records"
    max: "return config.maxRecords || 100"
files.config.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [baseId, tableId]
  properties:
    baseId:
      type: string
      title: Base ID
      description: Airtable Base ID, starts with 'app'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    tableId:
      type: string
      title: Table Name or ID
      description: Table name, e.g. 'Companies', or table ID starting with 'tbl'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    filterFormula:
      type: string
      title: Filter Formula (optional)
      description: An Airtable formula, e.g. NOT({Status}='Done')
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    fields:
      type: string
      title: Fields (optional)
      description: Comma-separated field names to return. Blank returns all fields.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    view:
      type: string
      title: View (optional)
      description: Name or ID of a view, which applies its own filters and sorts
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    sortField:
      type: string
      title: Sort Field (optional)
      description: Field name to sort by
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    sortDirection:
      type: string
      title: Sort Direction
      enum: [asc, desc]
      default: asc
      "ui:dependencies": { sortField: true }
    maxRecords:
      type: number
      title: Max Records
      description: Stop after this many. Pages are fetched automatically until reached.
      default: 100
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 5000
    dedupField:
      type: string
      title: Dedup Field (optional)
      description: Keep only the first record for each distinct value of this field
      default: ""
"ui:order":
  [baseId, tableId, filterFormula, fields, view, sortField, sortDirection, maxRecords, dedupField]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: Trigger. Config values may template from upstream output.

outputs:
  - name: records
    type: array
    description: The records, each a plain object of its fields plus its Airtable `id`
  - name: totalCount
    type: number
    description: How many records came back after paging and dedup

credentials:
  - name: airtableCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Airtable
files.node.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/node.schema.json

type: AirtableFetch
kind: PromiseNode
name: Airtable Fetch
category: Storage & Data
color: "#FCB400"
description: Read records from an Airtable table, with filters, views, sorting and paging
whenToUse: >
  Pick to READ rows out of an Airtable table: filtered, sorted, from a named view, and
  paged automatically past the first hundred. Returns the records as plain objects with
  their Airtable id. Use it when the data lives in Airtable rather than a database.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # Idempotent read. The table can change underneath, so this is eligible rather than free:
  # memoization is off engine-wide by default.
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/test.schema.json

# Needs a real base. Point baseId and tableId at one you own before running the bench.
testData:
  config:
    baseId: appXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
    tableId: Companies
    filterFormula: ""
    fields: ""
    view: ""
    sortField: ""
    sortDirection: asc
    maxRecords: 5
    dedupField: ""
  inputs:
    input: {}
  expect:
    records: "return Array.isArray(output.records)"
    totalCount: "return output.totalCount === output.records.length"
